methodological_rigor.justification: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 36 retrospective cohort studies (6,839 patients) follows a rigorous systematic search across 10 databases with dual-reviewer data extraction and NOS quality assessment. Random-effects models are appropriately used for all comparisons. Heterogeneity is quantified with I2 and chi-square tests, sensitivity analyses are performed, and publication bias is evaluated with funnel plots. The main limitation is the reliance on retrospective cohort studies due to absence of RCTs, significant cirrhosis imbalance between groups, and documented publication bias. No prospective controlled trial exists to compare.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a systematic review of retrospective cohort studies, mapping to Oxford LoE 2a. The findings have direct clinical relevance: LT versus LR for HCC within Milan criteria is an active clinical debate, and the quantitative pooling of 36 studies with nearly 7,000 patients provides robust comparative evidence informing treatment selection. The significantly better 3-, 5-, and 10-year OS and DFS rates for LT translate to actionable guidance for transplant-eligible patients.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript follows PRISMA guidelines with a PRISMA flow diagram, systematic search strategy in multiple databases, dual-reviewer extraction, NOS quality scoring, and heterogeneity assessment. Search terms are reported and the time frame is specified. Funnel plots assess publication bias. Limitations include heterogeneity in surgical approaches across centers, incomplete follow-up data in some included studies. The protocol was not pre-registered and no data availability statement for extracted data is provided.

novelty_literature.justification: LT versus LR meta-analyses for HCC within the Milan criteria have been published previously (including Zheng et al 2014 cited in the paper). While this study adds more recent data (search to June 2024) and includes 10 databases including Chinese language sources, it is an update and expansion rather than a fundamentally novel contribution. The conclusions align with prior systematic reviews. The addition of 10-year OS and DFS data from 5 studies provides marginal incremental value.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured with clear methods, results organized by outcome timepoint, and a comprehensive discussion contextualizing heterogeneity sources. Limitations are explicitly addressed including the lack of RCTs, selection bias, and publication bias. The clinical implications are clearly stated. Some sections in the discussion repeat content from the results, and the extensive discussion of organ shortage and healthcare systems, while relevant, could be condensed.

key_strengths: Comprehensive search across 10 databases including Chinese language literature with 36 studies and 6,839 patients
Consistent LT superiority across multiple time points (3, 5, 10-year OS; all DFS intervals; recurrence rate) provides robust comparative evidence
Sensitivity analyses and NOS quality scoring add methodological rigor
key_concerns: Significant cirrhosis severity imbalance between LT and LR groups (more Child-Pugh B/C in LT) creates inherent confounding that may overestimate LT benefit
All included studies are retrospective cohort studies with documented funnel plot asymmetry indicating publication bias
The 10-year OS analysis includes only 5 studies with high heterogeneity (I2=67%) limiting the reliability of long-term conclusions
No protocol pre-registration (PROSPERO) which is standard for systematic reviews
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed meta-analysis updating LT versus LR evidence for HCC within the Milan criteria, appropriate for a Tier 3 journal. The inherent confounding from patient selection differences and publication bias are acknowledged but unavoidable, and the clinical message is clear and well-supported.
